mediumOfInstruction: Pre-primary targets English and French, scaffolded on the child's first language
The framework names that L1 only as the child's first language, never which one
Ombudsperson quotes Education Regulations s.43: in Standards IV to VI the medium is English
Up to and including Standard III any one language may be employed as the medium
The Minister decides which language that is, as most suitable for the pupils

evidence.bullet: Pre-primary targets English and French, scaffolded on the child's first language
evidence.quote: The CLL programme aims to develop the emergent skills in communicating, listening, speaking, reading, and writing in English and French (target languages), scaffolded on their first language (L1).

evidence.bullet: The framework names that L1 only as the child's first language, never which one
evidence.quote: and writing in English and French (target languages), scaffolded on their first language (L1).

evidence.bullet: Ombudsperson quotes Education Regulations s.43: in Standards IV to VI the medium is English
evidence.quote: In Standards IV, V, and VI of the Government and aided primary schools the medium of instruction shall be English, and conversation between teacher and pupils shall be carried on in English

evidence.bullet: Up to and including Standard III any one language may be employed as the medium
evidence.quote: In the lower classes of Government and aided primary schools up to and including Standard III, any one language may be employed as the language of instruction

evidence.bullet: The Minister decides which language that is, as most suitable for the pupils
evidence.quote: being a language which in the opinion of the Minister is most suitable for the pupils

sources.label: Mauritius Institute of Education, National Curriculum Framework Pre-Primary (2024), section 4.2 Communication, Language and Literacy

Ombudsperson for Children (Mauritius), 'Case 3: Kreol language in the education system', quoting Education Regulations s.43 'Medium of instruction and teaching of languages' — reproduced in full by LALIT; the Regulations themselves are not published on attorneygeneral.govmu.org or lawsofmauritius.govmu.org, and the Education Act carries no medium provision
